name: Tubular CT cavity candidates
mask_semantics: Selected mineralized material is 1; background or CT void is 0.

survey.display_selection: Longest sampled principal centrelines among the qualified candidates.

method: Inward signed-volume mesh components propose local envelopes. Face-connected voids touching the padded crop boundary are rejected. The closest sealed component within two native samples of each envelope face is thinned with the Lee algorithm. Connected skeleton paths are sampled between extremal coordinates; the longest measured path is retained. Every trace node is independently checked against the original zero-valued mask.
native_diameter_estimator: Twice the median Euclidean distance from traced voxel centres to the nearest selected-material voxel centre. A discrete geometric estimate on the 18 µm sampling grid.
display: Interactive X-ray tube sweep along voxel centres. A visible minimum diameter of 0.16 mm in native CT coordinates can exaggerate thin candidates. Measured diameters remain unmodified in this record.
interpretation: These are candidate tubular CT voids. The chosen subset excludes surface-connected channels, structures outside the tested bounds, and cavities with ambiguous paths. It does not identify vasculature, dentinal tubules, material composition, or a complete biological network.

literature_context.title: Micro-computed tomography imaging reveals the development of a unique tooth mineralization pattern in mackerel sharks
Dental pathologies in lamniform and carcharhiniform sharks

registration: The same native lattice is translated from the MHA patient origin to the registered web mesh origin. The viewer then applies its documented display affine.
